strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Closes the reopened semantic protocol/event contract blocker with a Runtime-owned generated contract, golden Rust-to-VSIX fixture tests, and guard-enforced drift detection so external controllers can depend on stable request/result semantics.
Keeps protocol semantics, unknown-field rejection, enum handling, and durable event migration coupling inside Runtime/protocol/store authority rather than CLI, VSIX, prose, or model output.
Preserves controlled JSON-RPC and MCP tool execution boundaries by making public Runtime params fail closed on unknown fields while leaving tool execution authority in Rust Runtime.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, and controlled_workspace_tools by closing RRP-5.1 semantic protocol/event contract evidence with Rust-generated contract artifacts and VSIX golden tests.
answers.new_capability: The repository now has a machine-readable Runtime-owned semantic protocol contract generated by brownie-protocol, checked for freshness, and consumed by VSIX tests for request projection and validator behavior.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: RRP-5 ownership mapping detected missing methods/events and source drift, but it did not prove required/optional/null/enum semantics, Rust serialization, VSIX projection compatibility, unknown-field rejection, or durable event migration coupling.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A headless controller could see a method listed as owned while Rust and VSIX disagree on field names, optional/null behavior, enum values, or unknown-field policy, leaving release compatibility unproven.
answers.non_duplicative: This is the RRP-5.1 semantic contract corrective; it does not repeat RRP-4.1 durable migration recovery, RRP-7.1 deadline/failure injection work, RRP-6 module decomposition, or direct CI workflow hardening.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. RRP-5.1 adds no JSON-RPC method and instead defines/checks the semantics of existing public Runtime methods.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The new JSON artifact is release evidence generated by Rust protocol code, not a runtime diagnostic endpoint, report wrapper, dashboard, or user-facing summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Public Rust protocol params for key Runtime methods now use serde deny_unknown_fields, making malformed over-broad request payloads fail closed; VSIX tests lock the client projection to the generated Rust contract.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless automation gets stable machine-checked protocol semantics across Runtime and VSIX, reducing accidental compatibility drift before autonomous release operation depends on these boundaries.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes protocol-event-canonization while keeping Runtime Release Ready false until platform-deadline-durability-hardening, runtime-release-guard-ci, and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.

implementation_audit_classification.evidence: brownie-protocol::semantic_contract owns runtime-semantic-protocol-contract-v1 and the brownie-protocol-semantic-contract binary writes/checks docs/architecture/runtime-semantic-protocol-contract.json.
Rust tests check artifact freshness, unknown-field rejection for key Runtime params, and fixture equivalence to Rust serialization for task.start, task.cancel, task.run, and TaskStatus.
VSIX tests read the generated artifact, validate fixture shapes, reject unknown fields, and prove task.start camelCase client input becomes snake_case Rust wire params.
The semantic contract and guard bind event-shape changes to brownie-store schema migration policy and store schema version 2 evidence.
The phase does not set runtime_release_ready=true, change license/publish/release metadata, start hosted platform work, or modify .github workflow files.

semantic contract is not generated or checked by Rust brownie-protocol code
Rust and VSIX golden fixtures do not prove request/result semantics and task.start projection
unknown-field policy can drift open for public Runtime params
durable event shape changes are not coupled to store schema migration policy
guard:protocol-event-canonization stops requiring RRP-5.1 semantic evidence

CLI, VSIX, external controller state, prose, model output, raw prompts, provider output, file contents, paths, secrets, environment values, executable content, or process output are treated as Runtime authority

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-5.1 changes guard-engine files, current phase manifest, canonical protocol/event map, and Runtime release-readiness audit while closing protocol-event-canonization. Review must confirm the Rust-generated semantic contract is freshness-checked, VSIX golden tests prove client projection and validator semantics, unknown-field and enum policies fail closed, durable event changes remain migration-coupled, and Runtime Release Ready remains false.

exit_criteria: docs/architecture/runtime-semantic-protocol-contract.json is generated by brownie-protocol and checked for freshness.
Rust tests prove artifact freshness, unknown-field rejection, enum values, and fixture serialization semantics.
VSIX tests consume the generated artifact and prove validators reject unknown fields plus task.start projection matches Rust wire params.
guard:protocol-event-canonization fails when generated contract, unknown-field evidence, VSIX tests, or durable migration coupling are removed.
protocol-event-canonization is closed while Runtime Release Ready remains false and platform-deadline-durability-hardening plus runtime-release-guard-ci remain open.

accepted_capability: Rust protocol crate owns and generates the semantic protocol contract artifact.
VSIX validates generated golden fixtures and projection semantics against that artifact.
Public Runtime params covered by RRP-5.1 reject unknown fields in Rust and VSIX evidence.
Durable event changes remain coupled to explicit store schema migration policy.
behavior_evidence: Rust semantic_contract tests cover generator freshness and serde semantics.
VSIX semanticProtocolContract tests cover validators and request projection.
guard:protocol-event-canonization and its tests enforce RRP-5.1 evidence through the existing VSIX check path.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime/protocol/store remain execution, admission, replay, permission, MCP, workspace mutation, durable state, protocol, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection clients and cannot grant Runtime authority.
Raw prompt, provider output, file content, absolute/canonical path, secret, environment value, executable content, and process output are not persisted as release evidence.
non_goals: Does not claim Runtime Release Ready.
Does not change license, publish settings, tags, release assets, or public OSS release posture.
Does not add hosted scheduler, daemon, worker fleet, queue, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, remote Git expansion, signing infrastructure, or external platform products.
Does not modify .github workflow files; runtime-release-guard-ci remains a separate blocker.
Does not close platform-deadline-durability-hardening cross-platform or Runtime-wide deadline debt.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected docs-only closure because semantic compatibility needs generated fixtures and executable tests.
Rejected VSIX-owned schema generation because Runtime/protocol must own public wire semantics.
Rejected adding new RPCs because the closure concerns existing protocol compatibility.
technical_debt: platform-deadline-durability-hardening remains required-before-release for Runtime-wide persisted deadlines and cross-platform hardening.
runtime-release-guard-ci remains open Runtime-owned debt until workflow-scope credentials or owner-approved equivalent CI hardening exists.
Owner license/publish/release decisions remain required before OSS Release Ready.
next_capability_rationale: Return to runtime-release-guard-ci only when workflow-scope credentials or an owner-approved equivalent path is available; otherwise continue bounded audits while platform/deadline/cross-platform debt remains explicitly open.

runtime_release_dod: RRP-5.1 closes protocol-event-canonization with generated semantic evidence while keeping broader release readiness blocked by platform/deadline/durability and CI release-gate items.
Runtime Release Ready remains false until remaining Runtime blockers and owner license/publish/release decisions are resolved.
runtime_boundary_contracts: No new RPC surface is added; existing Runtime JSON-RPC and ledger semantics are preserved and more strictly checked.
CLI and VSIX remain thin clients over Runtime-owned contracts.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: External scheduling, queueing, worker leases, hosted isolation, retry policy, metrics, alerts, SLA, tenant administration, billing, and secret-provider operations remain outside this local Runtime v0 phase.
external_adapter_responsibilities: Forge, pull request, review, notification, SIEM, OTel, language verifier, customer integration, and hosted MCP adapter responsibilities remain outside RRP-5.1.
commercial_solution_readiness: Packaging, distribution, signing, notarization, enterprise administration, operational runbooks, support, and commercial release decisions remain out of scope.
Cargo license and publish settings remain owner-decision items and are not changed by RRP-5.1.
